Description: Chemically synthesized low-molecular-weight medicines, including oral and injectable small-molecule drugs.
Include_Keywords: small molecule|oral therapy|kinase inhibitor|chemical entity|NCE|SGLT2|JAK inhibitor|BTK inhibitor
Reviewer_Notes: Use Y when the company has meaningful marketed products, active pipeline assets, or a stated strategic capability in small molecules.

Description: Antibody-based therapies designed to bind a single target antigen.
Include_Keywords: monoclonal antibody|mAb|antibody therapy|IgG|fully human antibody|humanized antibody
Reviewer_Notes: Use Y for conventional single-target antibody franchises or active antibody pipelines. Bispecifics and ADCs should also be separately flagged where relevant.

Description: Antibody therapies engineered to bind two targets or epitopes.
Reviewer_Notes: Use Y only when bispecific antibody products or active bispecific pipeline assets are visible.

Description: Antibody-drug conjugates combining antibody targeting with a linked cytotoxic or therapeutic payload.
Reviewer_Notes: Use Y where ADC is a marketed product, active pipeline area, or explicitly highlighted strategic platform.

Description: Preventive or therapeutic vaccines, including protein, viral vector, mRNA, conjugate, and inactivated vaccine approaches.
Include_Keywords: vaccine|immunization|immunisation|conjugate vaccine|viral vector vaccine|protein vaccine|preventive vaccine|therapeutic vaccine
Reviewer_Notes: Use Y for companies with meaningful vaccine franchises, active vaccine pipelines, or dedicated vaccine platforms. mRNA vaccines should also be flagged under mRNA.

Description: Messenger RNA-based medicines or vaccines using mRNA as the active therapeutic or antigen-encoding component.
Reviewer_Notes: Use Y for companies with marketed mRNA products, active mRNA pipeline assets, or explicit mRNA platform strategy.

Description: Cell-based therapies, including autologous or allogeneic CAR-T, TCR, NK-cell, stem-cell, and other engineered cell approaches.
Include_Keywords: cell therapy|CAR-T|CAR T|TCR therapy|NK cell|stem cell therapy|allogeneic cell|autologous cell
Reviewer_Notes: Use Y for active or marketed cell therapy exposure. Do not mark Y for basic cell biology research without a therapeutic platform or asset.

Description: Gene replacement, gene addition, gene editing, or vector-based genetic medicines.
Include_Keywords: gene therapy|gene editing|AAV|lentiviral vector|CRISPR|base editing|gene replacement
Reviewer_Notes: Use Y for marketed or active gene therapy and gene editing assets. Cell therapies with gene modification can be flagged under both Cell_Therapy and Gene_Therapy if strategically meaningful.

Description: Non-mRNA RNA-targeting or RNA-based therapeutics such as siRNA, antisense oligonucleotides, RNAi, and splice-modulating therapies.
Reviewer_Notes: Keep separate from mRNA because the platform logic and companies involved can differ.

Description: Therapeutic proteins, peptides, enzymes, hormones, and recombinant biologics that are not primarily antibodies.
Example_Products_or_Assets: insulin analogues|GLP-1 peptides|enzyme replacement therapies|coagulation factors
Reviewer_Notes: Useful for companies with diabetes, obesity, rare disease enzyme replacement, or recombinant protein franchises.

Description: Biologic products highly similar to already-approved reference biologics.
Reviewer_Notes: Use Y for companies with meaningful biosimilar commercial or pipeline exposure.

Description: Off-patent small-molecule medicines or generic drug portfolios.
Reviewer_Notes: Use Y only when generics are a meaningful part of the company's business model, not just legacy minor exposure.

Description: Diagnostic tests, imaging agents, companion diagnostics, assay platforms, or diagnostic devices.
Example_Products_or_Assets: companion diagnostics|imaging diagnostics|in vitro diagnostic platforms
Reviewer_Notes: Use Y for diagnostics-focused companies or therapeutic companies with meaningful diagnostic/imaging business exposure.

Description: Medical devices, drug-device combinations, delivery devices, monitoring devices, or connected therapeutic hardware.
Example_Products_or_Assets: insulin pens|inhalers|continuous monitoring devices|drug delivery devices
Reviewer_Notes: Use Y only when device exposure is a meaningful commercial or strategic element.

Description: Life-science tools, bioprocessing, CDMO, manufacturing platforms, research reagents, or enabling technology services.
Include_Keywords: CDMO|CMO|manufacturing|bioprocessing|life science tools|research tools|reagents|contract development|contract manufacturing
Reviewer_Notes: Important for companies such as Lonza or Danaher that do not fit a pure therapeutics modality model.

Description: Material modality exposure that does not fit the current controlled vocabulary.
Exclude_Keywords: use a more specific modality when available
Reviewer_Notes: Use sparingly and add a Reviewer_Notes explanation. Consider adding a new modality if repeated across companies.
